newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks seen hovering in narrow range.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks seen hovering in narrow range.

text.p: The Tokyo stock market's key index is expected to hover in a narrow range on Friday, as selling pressure between 20,500 and 21,000 is likely to block any rise, brokers said.

The market will be cautious about the yen's climb against the dollar overnight, as any further rise will hurt shares of leading exporters. It is also waiting for the U.S. employment data, a key U.S. economic indicator, due out later today.
On Thursday, the 225-share Nikkei average shed 123.41 points or 0.60 percent to finish at 20,488.15. Its June futures slipped 80 yen to finish at 20,470.
"I expect the Nikkei 225 to hover within 50 points above and below yesterday's close," said Kenji Karikomi, deputy general manager at Daiwa Securities Co Ltd.
"People are likely to be nervous about the yen, which looks to have a slightly upward bias," said a broker at a medium-sized securities house.
The dollar traded at 115.50/60 yen in early Asia trade on Friday, against 115.87/92 yen in late Tokyo trade on Thursday.
